name: Do I need a permit for an attached patio cover in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for an attached patio cover if it is small or simple?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit for an attached patio cover if it is small or simple?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the patio cover attaches to the house, plan on a permit in most Los Angeles-area jurisdictions. The main exception is usually a small detached accessory structure under 120 square feet, but once the cover is connected to the dwelling, it is typically treated as permitted construction. The exact requirement can also depend on the city, zoning, setbacks, and whether the project includes electrical, plumbing, or structural modifications. Before building, confirm whether the property is in the City of Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, North Hollywood, or unincorporated county territory, because local rules can differ. A contractor or designer should verify size, attachment method, and any special review triggers before fabrication starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. In Los Angeles County, an attached patio cover generally requires a building permit even when the design is simple. Detached accessory structures under 120 square feet may be exempt, but attachment to the home usually changes the permit requirement.
